issues.description: The solution implements Animal and concrete animal constructors that take (String name, int age) and the Animal class in the solution contains an additional age attribute. However, the problem statement UML and the template's Main use/expect single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")) and the UML only shows a name attribute for Animal. This mismatch between the expected constructor signatures in the template/problem and the solution will confuse students about how to declare/instantiate the animal classes and which attributes must be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures and attributes consistent across problem, template, and solution. Option A (preferred for minimal change): update the solution to provide single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal and all concrete animals and remove the extra age attribute (or make an overloaded constructor if age is optional). Option B: if age is intended to be part of the design, update the problem statement UML and the template Main to require/illustrate two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and document the age attribute in the instructions.
